mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a correct set‑builder description of the set {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}?

options.A: {x | x is an even natural number less than 12}
options.B: {x | x is a natural number and 2 ≤ x ≤ 10}
options.C: {x | x ∈ ℕ and x is divisible by 2 and x ≤ 10}
options.D: {x | x is a positive integer and x is a multiple of 2 less than 12}

mcqs.answer: {x | x is a natural number and 2 ≤ x ≤ 10}
mcqs.explanation: Option B includes all natural numbers from 2 to 10, which also contains odd numbers (3,5,7,9) that are not in the given set. The other options correctly restrict x to even numbers only, matching {2,4,6,8,10}.

mcqs.question: The set S = {x | x is an integer and –3 ≤ x ≤ 3}. Which of the following is the roster form of S?
mcqs.explanation: The set‑builder condition lists every integer from –3 up to 3 inclusive, giving exactly the seven elements shown in option A. Options B, C, and D omit some required elements.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a finite set from an infinite set?

options.A: A finite set can be listed completely in roster form, while an infinite set cannot be listed completely in roster form.
options.B: A finite set always has a set‑builder description, while an infinite set cannot be described using set‑builder form.
options.C: A finite set contains only natural numbers, while an infinite set contains real numbers.
options.D: A finite set has a greatest element, while an infinite set has no elements.

mcqs.answer: A finite set can be listed completely in roster form, while an infinite set cannot be listed completely in roster form.
mcqs.explanation: Finite sets have a limited number of elements, so they can be enumerated explicitly (roster). Infinite sets have endlessly many elements, making a complete roster impossible. Options B, C, and D give false statements about set‑builder capability, element types, and existence of elements.

mcqs.question: Let A = {x ∈ ℤ | x² ≤ 9}. Which of the following is the most concise description of set A?

options.C: {x | x is a natural number and x ≤ 9}
options.D: {x | x is a real number and x² ≤ 9}

mcqs.explanation: The condition x² ≤ 9 for integers is equivalent to saying the absolute value of x is at most 3, which is captured succinctly in option B. Option A lists the elements but is longer; C restricts to natural numbers only; D allows all real numbers, which would include non‑integers such as 2.5.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the roster form of the set of vowels in the English alphabet?
mcqs.explanation: The vowels are a, e, i, o, u, and roster notation lists each element separately inside braces, as shown in option A. Option B lists consonants, C mixes vowels and consonants, and D is not proper roster notation.

mcqs.question: How would you express the set of all natural numbers greater than 5 using set‑builder notation?
mcqs.explanation: Set‑builder notation requires specifying the domain (ℕ for natural numbers) and the condition (n > 5). Option A does exactly that. Option B is roster‑style, C uses integers (including negatives), and D includes 5 itself.

mcqs.question: The set T = {2, 4, 6, 8}. Which of the following is an equivalent set‑builder description?

options.A: { x | x is an even natural number and x ≤ 8 }
options.B: { x | x is a natural number and x < 10 }
options.C: { x | x is a multiple of 2 }
options.D: { x | x ∈ ℝ and x is even }

mcqs.answer: { x | x is an even natural number and x ≤ 8 }
mcqs.explanation: T consists of the even natural numbers up to 8, which is precisely captured by option A. Option B also includes odd numbers (1,3,5,7,9), C includes all even numbers (infinitely many), and D allows non‑integer even real numbers.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets is infinite?
mcqs.explanation: The interval (0,1) contains infinitely many real numbers, making option B infinite. Options A, C, and D list a limited number of elements, so they are finite.
